endorsements.quote: The risk of AI-generated errors or culturally inappropriate content requires continuous human oversight and the ability to correct or override AI recommendations.
Healthcare organizations should adopt a phased, evidence-based approach to AI integration.

Drawing on Park’s “Sweet Spot” logic, oversight intensity increases as patient vulnerability, content sensitivity, or AI uncertainty increases―operationalized as explicit decision gates (approve/edit/reject) and a stop-escalation pathway ( Figure 1 ) (3) , (4) .
This necessitates comprehensive training programs for healthcare professionals and dedicated support systems for older adults and their families.
Verified patient data are curated into a clinician-approved “memory set” used for grounded drafting.
For pilots, a minimal evaluation set should include safety (distress/adverse events), effectiveness (engagement/therapeutic goals), and equity (performance across subgroups) (5) .
no patient-facing content is delivered without nurse approval.
Nurses, with their holistic understanding of patient needs, ethical grounding, and direct patient contact, are uniquely positioned to lead AI integration in RT.

unlisted_practices: Implement robust data encryption and secure storage protocols for AI systems handling sensitive patient information.
Provide opt-in/opt-out consent options for sensing and data use in AI-assisted therapy.
Maintain audit logs of AI-suggested, edited, and delivered content to support accountability and incident review.
Configure AI to default to confirm-before-assert behavior and hard stops when outputs are ungrounded or low confidence.
Pause AI-generated content and escalate to human-led judgment when patients are at high risk of distress, verified materials are insufficient, or the system signals low confidence.
Keep AI use optional and reversible and frame it as support for, not a substitute for, therapeutic relationships.
Run clinical trials comparing AI-assisted interventions with traditional methods, measuring safety, algorithmic transparency, and cost-effectiveness.
Set prespecified safety stop criteria for AI pilots.
Establish regulatory standards for content accuracy, privacy protection, and clinical oversight of AI in psychosocial interventions.
Design AI with user-centered features such as voice commands, simplified controls, and culturally appropriate interfaces.
Provide digital coach programs and ongoing technical support for older adults and their families using AI tools.
